newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy to visit South America.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to visit South America.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's special envoy, Thomas McLarty, will visit South America at the weekend to press strong U.S. support for advancing the agenda of the 1994 Summit of the Americas, the State Department said Wednesday.
McLarty, Clinton's close friend and adviser, will travel to Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay Nov. 16 to 23.

During the trip, McLarty will discuss bilateral and regional issues with the three countries' presidents and senior officials and will offer them an outline of Clinton's second term agenda for the western hemisphere, deputy spokesman Glyn Davies said.

McLarty plans two major speeches on administration policy priorities during his travels. The first will be on Nov. 18 at a conference in Sao Paulo, Brazil. The second will be on Nov. 20 at a lunch hosted by the American-Argentina Chamber of Commerce in Buenos Aires.
McLarty will also discuss with government and business leaders development of the agenda for the next Summit of the Americas in Santiago, Chile in early 1998.

The summits were initiated by Clinton. The inaugural one -- held in Miami in December 1994 -- was the first among Latin American leaders in 27 years and set plans to create the world's largest free trade zone by the year 2005. It also mapped out plans for cooperation on other issues, including efforts against money laundering and narcotics trafficking.
